$comment: What can be run in this repository, and what each thing means (rule:work-legibility). Read by the Chain tool; useful to a person either way. `reaches` is mandatory whenever the target is not `local`. NOTE: many entries share `verify/unit@local` — that is correct, because the axis says how DEEP a run reaches, not what kind it is. The kind (lint, tests, typecheck, audit) comes from the command itself and is shown as the subtype; the declaration does not have to repeat it.

entrypoints.$comment: Reads a local lockfile but consults the RustSec advisory database over the network. Target stays `local`: nothing of this project leaves the machine.
The whole gate: every verify/unit entry above, in one run. `integration` because it crosses both runtimes — a green tsc plus a green cargo test is a statement about the pair, not about either alone.
The development channel. NOT a release, and never to be called one (rule:live-app).

Produces the installable bundle. The only correct way to build a release — a bare `tauri build` inherits TAURI_CONFIG from a dev shell and silently builds against the dev identity (rule:live-app). Installing it is the maintainer's act, never an agent's.
Pulls the pinned upstream layers. Reaches a remote, so it declares it — even though nothing of this project goes out.
`prod` because pushed history is public and permanent. Gated by the pre-push hook running check:all (rule:automation).
A tag triggers the cross-platform release build. Only on the maintainer's explicit word (rule:versioning).
